transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/time: 2026-06-17 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~43 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Mark Chen (Lead ML Eng, Aurelia), Priya Desai (Head of AI, Aurelia), Roberto Gomez (Infra), Aisha Khan (Product)

Summary (auto): quick weekly poc sync. Reviewed benchmark runs Redwood vs baseline provider (BaselineCorp). Discussed p95 latency, throughput, batching, kv cache, quantization tradeoffs, networking/VPC. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics: benchmark summary, tuning levers (batching, quant, cache), networking/VPC test plan, security docs, next steps/exec review

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Lena: ok everyone, thanks for joining, starting recording. quick agenda: recap last week's runs, share today's numbers versus baseline, then dig into tuning and next steps.
[00:00:22] Mark: yep thanks Lena, we've got Priya and Roberto on as well, Mark here. we ran the baseline on our infra monday, matched your sample payloads.
[00:00:35] Samir: cool. just to set context, today's numbers are from the dedicated pool with the 80B quantized variant, continuous batching on, k-v cache warm. baseline's numbers are what you sent from BaselineCorp.
[00:00:48] Priya: quick question, samir, that 80B quantized — is that int8 or int4-ish? we saw mention of q4 in the notes.
[00:00:56] Samir: yeah it's q4_0 for these runs, we did a secondary q8-ish for throughput sanity but the primary is q4. so expect slightly lower quality but big perf gains.
[00:01:12] Roberto: just flag — our staging has different seq lengths, we usually hit 2k median, but for the stress test we're doing 8k to exercise kv.
[00:01:22] Lena: right which is why we ran both 2k and 8k. quick high level: Redwood p95 latency on 8k seq was ~410ms versus BaselineCorp at ~520ms — so about 20% better p95. throughput (tokens/sec) about 1.25x higher on average.
[00:01:45] Mark: that's promising, can you show the p95 distribution? the spreadsheet had averages but not tail.
[00:01:53] Samir: sure, i can walk through. (screen share noises) so here's the histogram — a small bump at 95-98th from cache misses, most of that is network— um, actually we saw some warmup issues where the k v cache wasn't fully warm on certain hosts, so p99 jumps.
[00:02:20] Mark: when you say 'k v' cache the transcript had it as 'kv' earlier — sorry..
[00:02:25] Samir: yeah k-v cache, the key-value cache for attention. it's per-host and we observed a ~15-20ms penalty on cache miss.
[00:02:33] Priya: and what about batching? you mentioned continuous batching, what's the target batch size?
[00:02:39] Samir: default target batch 64 for these runs, dynamic batching up to 128 if latency SLO allows. We tuned batch windows to 20ms to keep p95 in range.
[00:02:53] Aisha: how does that compare to baseline provider's batching?
[00:02:58] Samir: baseline used fixed micro-batching at 32, but they had different autoscaler config which caused more variance. that's one of the reasons their throughput is lower.
[00:03:09] Roberto: network-wise, do you see egress spikes or retries? our infra folks saw occasional 5xx from the baseline provider test.
[00:03:17] Samir: our logs had occasional timeouts when we forced cross-region fallback, but for the dedicated pool in same region it was minimal. BaselineCorp's runs had a couple of sustained retries, which inflated p95.
[00:03:30] Mark: can you confirm request size and tokenization — were we using the same prompts and truncation rules?
[00:03:36] Lena: yes same prompt set as the baseline spreadsheet, we used identical tokenization and the same input trimming at 8k max. sample prompts are in the shared folder.
[00:03:48] Priya: quality wise — any loss with q4? some hallucination checks?
[00:03:53] Samir: we ran the eval set, minor differences in exact phrasing but overall hit the accuracy thresholds defined in the poc. We'll share the evaluation diff.
[00:04:05] Mark: good. can we dig into the 95th percentile stress plan — what are you proposing?
[00:04:10] Lena: propose running a 2-hour sustained run at 8k seq with randomized user sessions to warm k-v fully and measure p95/p99 under realistic traffic. samir will run and provide logs.
[00:04:22] Samir: yep, i'll do that, and i'll push a variant that disables prefetch to see impact on cache misses.
[00:04:30] Priya: perfect. on security — we need SOC2 details and KMS integration notes. also need confirmation on SAML SSO and audit logs retention.
[00:04:41] Lena: understood. i'll send the Redwood security pack — SOC2, ISO summary, KMS/HSM integration guide, and the audit log retention options. we can also provide a network diagram for the V P C peering.
[00:04:54] Roberto: on V P C — what's the typical peering pattern? do we do private peering, or is there a proxy? we need ip ranges for firewall rules.
[00:05:02] Samir: we support direct VPC peering and a private ingress option via our customer-managed NAT, we'll include both diagrams. ip ranges are in the doc i'll attach.
[00:05:12] Mark: any blocker on data residency? some of our workloads must stay in eu-central.
[00:05:17] Lena: we have region pinning and dedicated capacity can be provisioned in eu regions, we'll confirm capacity lead time.
[00:05:25] Aisha: pricing question — how does dedicated compare to hosted for sustained volume?
[00:05:29] Lena: dedicated is commit-based monthly; for your expected QPS from last week's sizing it becomes cost-effective around the 3-4 month horizon. i'll send a side-by-side.
[00:05:39] Priya: cool. BaselineCorp had a discount for longer commit, but their latency was worse — so we need to weigh cost vs tail latency.
[00:05:47] Samir: also note quality vs quant tradeoff — you can run a hybrid where we serve critical routes on q8 or fp16 and background on q4 to balance cost. we've done that for other finance customers.
[00:05:58] Mark: can you share a sample config for hybrid routing?
[00:06:02] Samir: yes i'll add that to the artifacts — routing policy example, canary config, and automatic fallback to a smaller model if capacity gets constrained.
[00:06:12] Lena: ok let's talk about the anomalies — we saw a p99 spike around minute 23 in the run. samir what was that?
[00:06:18] Samir: that was a cross-host gc on one of the nodes and a cache rebalancing event, we have mitigation: staggered host restarts and more aggressive prefetching.
[00:06:27] Roberto: is that something we can reproduce on-prem? because we may want to run a private deployment if we see host-level instability.
[00:06:33] Samir: you can reproduce with adversarial seq lengths but it's rare in normal traffic. private deployment with same runtime and pinned kernel selection avoids noisy multitenancy.
[00:06:43] Priya: what's the timeline to spin up dedicated in eu if we decide?
[00:06:46] Lena: typical lead time is 2-3 weeks to reserve capacity and run onboarding tests, potentially shorter if we have templated infra. we'll confirm by email.
[00:06:55] Mark: ok next steps — we want that long stress run and the logs. we also want the security pack and pricing.
[00:07:02] Lena: yep. Samir any more notes from the run?
[00:07:05] Samir: one more: we tested kernel selection changes — on A100 vs H100 there was a 10-15% diff on throughput. for your current Intel/AMD hosts the mapping will be different; we'll include a compatibility table.
[00:07:20] Priya: great, can you also include quantized quality deltas for our eval set?
[00:07:25] Samir: will do.
[00:07:28] Aisha: timeline for exec review — can we do 30 minutes next tuesday?
[00:07:33] Lena: works for me, i'll propose times after i attach docs.
[00:07:38] Mark: last question — any pre-reqs for VPC peering test? windows for firewall updates?
[00:07:44] Roberto: we typically need a maintenance window but small rules changes should be fine. i'll coordinate.
[00:07:50] Lena: perfect. i'll recap and send the sheet.
[00:07:55] (crosstalk)
[00:08:02] Lena: Recap: Redwood to run 2-hour 8k stress run and share p95/p99 logs; send SOC2/security pack and network diagrams; Samir to share batching/quant configs and kernel mapping; customer to run staging baseline and validate; schedule exec review.
[00:08:20] Priya: thanks all.
[00:08:22] Mark: thanks.
[00:08:25] Samir: thanks everyone.
[00:08:30] Lena: end recording.

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-transcriptions (k v vs kv, V P C spelled). Shared artifacts referenced: benchmark_spreadsheet.xlsx (link in chat), security_pack.zip (to be sent), routing_examples.md.

End of transcript.
